## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
*Uttaramātupetivatthu* ("Uttara’s Mother", Pv 22) is a text included in the *Petavatthu* collection of the Pali canon [SuttaCentral]. The core moral teaching of the work illustrates how harsh speech directed against those who do good deeds results in subsequent suffering [SuttaCentral]. SuttaCentral records four translations of the text in four languages [SuttaCentral].
Text-reuse analysis computed by DharmaNexus shows extensive internal Pali reuse with the commentary on the work, the *Petavatthu-aṭṭhakathā* (comprising 37 matches totaling 3,575 characters, with a primary shared segment across §3.6–10.4), as well as shared verses or prose segments with the sixth volume of the *Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā* (9 matches, notably around §7.4–8.2) [DharmaNexus]. In cross-language alignments, DharmaNexus detects tentative machine correspondences in Tibetan with the *Bodhisatvāvadānakalpalatā* (D4155-2) and the Kangyur text BO_K10_D0343_H0351, though these represent automatic alignments rather than established historical parallels [DharmaNexus].
*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on SuttaCentral and DharmaNexus data.*
